description: The typed question set, v2. Adds the 'edge' question for the multi-relational memory plane (validated in experiments/edges_v1 against the dual-model gold-v1). All v1 questions are carried verbatim; v1 remains on disk as the frozen historical set, and changing any question here is a version bump.

edge.instructions: In a memory graph of project constraints, what relation does record A bear to record B

criteria.supports: One record provides evidence, refinement, elaboration, or repetition for the other; following one reinforces or is consistent with the other
criteria.contradicts: Following both records is impossible; one forbids what the other requires, or they specify incompatible values for the same thing
criteria.supersedes: One record replaces the other due to a decision change, version update, or time passage; the replaced record is no longer intended to be followed
criteria.unrelated: The two records talk about different aspects, systems, or concerns; following one has no bearing on the other

edge.criteria_provenance: contracts/edge-schema.v1.json (frozen 2026-11-05); wire payload identical to the validated experiment question
edge.decision_rule: argmax of the returned probability map; p >= 0.80 proposes the edge, 0.50-0.79 routes to review

validation.observed: accuracy 115/117 (0.983); contradicts recall 5/5 and precision 5/5; unrelated recall 103/104; supports 7/8 both ways (n=8, directional); supersedes over-prediction 0; unstable pairs 1/117; both errors at p=0.5, which the decision_rule routes to review

relation.instructions: What is the relation between statement A and statement B

criteria.contradiction: Following both is impossible; one forbids what the other requires
criteria.complementary: Both can be true at once; one may refine or repeat the other
criteria.unrelated: They talk about different things and do not constrain each other

relation.decision_rule: argmax of the returned probability map

admit.instructions: Given the TASK, should this claim be admitted, reviewed, or excluded

criteria.admit: The claim constrains how the TASK must be done and is still in force
criteria.review: It is unclear whether the claim applies or still holds; a human must look
criteria.exclude: The claim does not constrain the TASK

admit.decision_rule: argmax of the returned probability map; on provider failure the record is review, never exclude

validation.note: Replaces the retired score = p(applies) x p(holds): one question instead of two, zero thresholds, no independence assumption.

contradiction.instructions: Two or more of the listed claims contradict each other for this TASK.
contradiction.decision_rule: descriptive; >= 0.70 forces review for every non-excluded record

governing.instructions: Which single claim should govern the TASK
governing.criteria_template: one option per candidate record (text truncated to 160 chars) plus 'none': No single claim governs this task
governing.decision_rule: confidence >= 0.80 promotes that record to admit; the contradiction field is still reported

validation.note: Exercised in scripts/jev_first_demo.py; no labelled measurement.

retired.name: applies
retired.why: Folded into 'admit'; keeping both required an independence assumption and a hand-made product to combine them.

cost_rule: One request per decision. The question count is the latency driver (10 questions measured 2.9-11.2 s), so candidate sets are capped at 6 records.
